results.content: We’re building something new at VoxMin. It’s called VoxMin Flo — an AI-native video creation platform designed around a simple idea: You shouldn’t need to learn filmmaking software to make a film. The attached podcast is actually created using VoxMin Flo. What we’re working on is making it ridiculously simple to go from an idea → characters → scenes → a complete video, whether that’s an AI movie, podcast, ad, short film, or something completely different. One thing we’ve been obsessing over is character consistency. Keeping the same characters, visual identity and context across multiple scenes is still one of the frustrating parts of AI video generation. We’re building Flo with that problem at the centre. And then there’s the other part we care about a lot: Cost. We run our generation [...] other part we care about a lot: Cost. We run our generation infrastructure on our own GPUs, which gives us significantly more control over inference costs. That means we can work towards making high-quality AI video genuinely affordable instead of something you experiment with once and then forget about because the bill hurts. 😄 We’re still a very small company. We don’t have the resources of the big players in this space. But that also means we get to move fast, experiment aggressively and build things the way we believe they should work. Our goal isn't to make AI video cheap. Affordable ≠ cheap. Affordable means lowering the barrier to creation while still respecting quality. There’s a long way to go with Flo. A lot will break before it gets good. But we’re excited about where this is [...] before it gets good. But we’re excited about where this is heading. Building quietly. Shipping constantly.
